lookback_source.quote: Review the medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

lookback_notes: The item's own pages state a 7-day look-back period for record review, staff interview, and observation. Per the general convention (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-21), a 7-day observation period consists of the ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days; the item's pages do not themselves describe the counting method.

coding_levels.label: Behavior not exhibited
coding_levels.definition: The behavioral symptoms were not present in the last 7 days. Use this code if the symptom has never been exhibited or if it previously has been exhibited but has been absent in the last 7 days.

source.quote: Code 0, behavior not exhibited: if the behavioral symptoms were not present in the last 7 days. Use this code if the symptom has never been exhibited or if it previously has been exhibited but has been absent in the last 7 days.

coding_levels.label: Behavior of this type occurred 1-3 days
coding_levels.definition: The behavior was exhibited 1-3 days of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any one of those days.

source.quote: Code 1, behavior of this type occurred 1-3 days: if the behavior was exhibited 1-3 days of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any one of those days.

coding_levels.label: Behavior of this type occurred 4-6 days, but less than daily
coding_levels.definition: The behavior was exhibited 4-6 of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

source.quote: Code 2, behavior of this type occurred 4-6 days, but less than daily: if the behavior was exhibited 4-6 of the last 7 days, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

coding_levels.label: Behavior of this type occurred daily
coding_levels.definition: The behavior was exhibited daily, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

source.quote: Code 3, behavior of this type occurred daily: if the behavior was exhibited daily, regardless of the number or severity of episodes that occur on any of those days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: E0200 is coded in three sub-items: A. Physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others (e.g., hitting, kicking, pushing, scratching, grabbing, abusing others sexually); B. Verbal behavioral symptoms directed toward others (e.g., threatening others, screaming at others, cursing at others); C. Other behavioral symptoms not directed toward others (e.g., physical symptoms such as hitting or scratching self, pacing, rummaging, public sexual acts, disrobing in public, throwing or smearing food or bodily wastes, or verbal/vocal symptoms like screaming, disruptive sounds). Enter codes in boxes.

source.quote: A. Physical behavioral symptoms directed toward others (e.g., hitting, kicking, pushing, scratching, grabbing, abusing others sexually)

federal_coding_rules.rule: Note presence of symptoms and their frequency.

source.quote:
Behavioral Symptom - Presence and Frequency
Note presence of symptoms and their frequency

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code based on whether the symptoms occurred and not based on an interpretation of the behavior's meaning, cause or the assessor's judgment that the behavior can be explained or should be tolerated.

source.quote: Code based on whether the symptoms occurred and not based on an interpretation of the behavior's meaning, cause or the assessor's judgment that the behavior can be explained or should be tolerated.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code as present, even if staff have become used to the behavior or view it as typical or tolerable.

source.quote: Code as present, even if staff have become used to the behavior or view it as typical or tolerable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Behaviors in these categories should be coded as present or not present, whether or not they might represent a rejection of care.

source.quote: Behaviors in these categories should be coded as present or not present, whether or not they might represent a rejection of care.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Item E0200C does not include wandering.

source.quote: Item E0200C does not include wandering.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding for items in Section E; the section focuses on the resident's actions, not the intent of their behavior.

source.quote: Resident intent should not be taken into account when coding for items in this section.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A behavior that did not occur during the look-back period is coded 0, behavior not exhibited (example: rummaging behavior not observed or reported in the last 7 days is coded 0 for E0200C).

source.quote:
Coding: E0200C would be coded 0, behavior not exhibited.
Rationale: The behavior did not occur during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A single, isolated incident of a physical behavior directed toward others is coded 1 (1-3 days) even when a possible explanation for the behavior exists.

source.quote: Rationale: Throwing a tray was a physical behavior directed toward others. Although a possible explanation exists, the behavior is noted as present because it occurred.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Coding of E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C determines E0300: if all three are coded 0, E0300 is coded 0 and the assessor skips to E0800; if any is coded 1, 2, or 3, E0300 is coded 1 and E0500 and E0600 are completed.

source.quote: Code 0, no: if E0200A, E0200B, and E0200C all are coded 0, not present. Skip to Rejection of Care—Presence & Frequency item (E0800).

federal.criterion: Review of the resident's medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Review the medical record for the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Listed as step 1 of Steps for Assessment.

federal.criterion: Interview of staff, across all shifts and disciplines, as well as others who had close interactions with the resident during the 7-day look-back period, including family or friends who visit frequently or have frequent contact with the resident.

source.quote: Interview staff, across all shifts and disciplines, as well as others who had close interactions with the resident during the 7-day look-back period, including family or friends who visit frequently or have frequent contact with the resident.

federal.notes: Listed as step 2 of Steps for Assessment.

federal.criterion: Observation of the resident in a variety of situations during the 7-day look-back period.

federal.notes: Listed as step 3 of Steps for Assessment.

federal.criterion: Subsequent assessments and documentation can be compared to baseline to identify changes in the resident's behavior, including response to interventions.
